subQuestions.questionText:

A third-party program that extends the built-in functionality of an application or browser.

subQuestions.questionText:

subQuestions.memoText: Relational database (1 mark)

subQuestions.memoText: Ransomware (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText:

subQuestions.memoText: Copyright (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText:

subQuestions.questionText: A university called 'LearnMore' is currently receiving student applications for the new year. It has been suggested that the desktop computers in the administration building should be replaced. State TWO characteristics of a motherboard that should be considered when purchasing new desktop computers.
subQuestions.memoText: Any TWO ✓✓ (2 marks): type of ZIF socket; type of CPU supported / bus speed; type of chipset; types of slots; number of slots; available ports; number of DIMM/RAM slots; extra features (Wi-Fi / Bluetooth built-in); number of SATA ports; form factor / physical size; on-board features like NIC.

subQuestions.questionText: Except for the CPU, name ONE other component that will process data in a computer system.
subQuestions.memoText: GPU / Graphics card / Video card ✓ (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: The secondary storage capacity is an important consideration when purchasing devices. Give TWO examples of flash storage devices that could be used in the administration building.
subQuestions.memoText: Any TWO ✓✓ (2 marks): flash drive; SSD / M.2; memory card / SD card.

subQuestions.questionText: The IT department at the university suggested that cloud-based servers could be used for the administration department. Briefly explain what a cloud-based virtual server is.
subQuestions.memoText: It is a server hosted / based on the internet (online) ✓ that does not exist as a physical entity / only exists in software ✓. (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: Justify the use of cloud-based virtual servers.
subQuestions.memoText: Any TWO justifications ✓✓ (2 marks): accessibility / ubiquity – the server can be accessed at any location / any time using an internet connection; scalability – the server specifications can be adapted to suit the changing needs of the university; the server does not use local resources; the service provider takes responsibility for maintenance and software upgrading; outsourcing of skilled processes; improved server reliability / availability; lower total operational cost / affordability.

subQuestions.questionText: Software as a Service (SaaS) is currently used on the computers in the administration building. Except for the benefit of renting instead of buying software, state TWO other benefits of using SaaS.
subQuestions.memoText: Any TWO ✓✓ (2 marks): don't need to install software on the computers / easy setup; do not need to update software on the computers; no need for high-end computers as you only run the applications from the web browser; the SaaS company is responsible for storing data and backups; work from multiple devices / locations; takes up less local resources; collaboration features; scalability / ability to upgrade the SaaS model according to their needs. Do NOT accept renting / cost.

subQuestions.questionText: Some of the software being used requires licences. Motivate why acquiring a site licence is better than acquiring a single-user licence for each of the users.
subQuestions.memoText:
A site licence allows all the employees of the institution to use the same licence ✓ which is cheaper than buying individual licences ✓.
Any TWO concepts (2 marks): replaces the need for individual licences / all users use the same licence; leading to cost saving; leading to less administration.

subQuestions.questionText: Critical to the success of the institution is ensuring no downtime and that regular backups of important data at the university are made. Explain what a backup strategy is and how it can help prevent downtime at the university.
subQuestions.memoText:
A backup strategy ensures that regular copies of data are made ✓ that will prevent data loss ✓ and ensure quick recovery / restoring of data ✓ to prevent downtime.
Any THREE concepts (3 marks): creating copies of data; regular creation of back-ups / copies; to prevent data loss; data can be quickly recovered / restored.

subQuestions.questionText: A cloud storage service could be used to backup data off-site. State TWO disadvantages of using cloud storage to backup data off-site.
subQuestions.memoText: Any TWO ✓✓ (2 marks): internet access required to access storage; bandwidth issues – you need a large amount of bandwidth to back up large chunks of data; full data recovery could take some time; data costs associated with storing data off-site; security exposure; data may be lost if the company / service closes down.

subQuestions.questionText:
An Engineering Graphics and Design course, using AutoCAD as a drawing tool, is offered at the university. Give ONE term for the type of computer user associated with the course above by choosing a term from the list below:

    home office user;  power user;  mobile user;  small office user
subQuestions.memoText: Power user ✓ (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Data security is essential to safeguard computer systems at the university against malware threats. One such threat is a computer worm. State TWO characteristics of a computer worm.
subQuestions.memoText: Any TWO ✓✓ (2 marks): ability to replicate itself from one computer to another; creates back-doors for other threats to gain access to a computer system; uses weak areas in an application / operating system to spread; transfers over a network to other devices; emails itself to all the contacts in an email address book; uses a lot of system resources (slows down the machine); causes strain on network bandwidth; causes loss of data.

subQuestions.questionText: Explain why an antivirus product, rather than a firewall, will protect a system from being infected by a computer worm.
subQuestions.memoText:
Firewalls monitor and manage access to a network from other networks ✓ while an antivirus identifies / blocks / removes malware ✓.
Concepts (2 marks): a firewall monitors network traffic but does not always prevent the spread of malware; an antivirus identifies / removes malware.

subQuestions.questionText: The new computers will be equipped with solid-state drives which do not need to be defragmented to optimise performance. Discuss why there is no need to defragment a solid-state drive.
subQuestions.memoText: Any ONE motivation ✓✓ (2 marks): an SSD has no moving parts (2); an SSD is a type of electronic storage (2); the grouping / position of stored data doesn't influence access speed (2).

subQuestions.questionText:
A school governing body decided to invest funds in communication and network technologies to upgrade the network of the school. The school network layout connects a School server and Switch 1 (Computer lab – 40 PCs), Switch 2 (Principal's office – 2 PCs), Switch 3 (Administration office – 3 PCs), Switch 4 (School Block A – 26 PCs) and Switch 5 (School Block B – 35 PCs), with the switches connected to one another in series from Switch 1 to Switch 5.

Define the term network.
subQuestions.memoText:
A network is a group of interconnected devices ✓ that can communicate with each other ✓.
Concepts (2 marks): multiple devices that are connected; via a communication medium.

subQuestions.questionText: Why do you think the school will benefit from investing in modern communication and network technologies?
subQuestions.memoText: Any TWO reasons ✓✓ (2 marks): improved productivity; improved communication speed; improved reliability; increasing the capacity; supports more devices; supports modern online services; improved collaboration. Also accept any ONE reason with an explanation.

subQuestions.questionText: Identify and motivate the need for at least TWO components used in a LAN.
subQuestions.memoText:
2 × name of component ✓✓ + 2 × motivation ✓✓ (4 marks):
• Network Interface Card (NIC) (1) – a hardware component that connects a device to the network (1)
• Switch (1) – a networking device that connects multiple devices together in a local area network (1)
• Router / Modem (1) – to provide connection to the internet (1)
• Cabling / communication medium (1) – to carry signals / connect devices / nodes (1)
• Wireless Access Points (1) – to provide wireless access to a network (1)

subQuestions.label: 3.1.4(a)
subQuestions.questionText: The switches are connected to one another from the computer lab to Block B of the school (from Switch 1 to Switch 5). Describe a potential disadvantage of this layout.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any ONE problem ✓✓ (2 marks): failure of one device / switch can make other parts of the network inaccessible; multiple switches are connected in series (1), if any one of the switches fails it can disrupt other parts of the network (1); a single cable between network segments (1) can lead to congestion in the cables / loss of network management efficiency (1); the signal travels through multiple switches (1), which can slow down communication (1).
Concepts: switches connected in series / single cable between network segments / signal travels through multiple switches / a problem in one device influences other parts of the network; can lead to congestion / slower communication / network segments failing.

subQuestions.label: 3.1.4(b)
subQuestions.questionText: Draw a basic diagram to suggest an alternative layout for the network that will prevent the potential problem described in QUESTION 3.1.4(a).
subQuestions.memoText:
A star layout: a central switch / router ✓ with the secondary switches (Switch 1–4) each individually connected to it ✓.
Concepts (2 marks): centralised switch (1); secondary switches individually connected (1).

subQuestions.questionText: A network can be made up of wired and wireless communication media. Suggest ONE type of wireless technology that can be utilised in an extended network.
subQuestions.memoText: Any ONE ✓ (1 mark): WiFi / access points; range extenders; WiMax; satellite; mesh technology.

subQuestions.questionText: Explain how the wireless capability of the school's network can be extended to cover the entire school grounds.
subQuestions.memoText:
Using additional access points ✓ which can be placed strategically / spread across the school grounds ✓.
OR: WiMAX (1) has a larger range (1). Also accept other technically correct answers. (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: The school needs to provide network access to their hostel at another location about one kilometre away. Suggest a possible solution and indicate how your solution would solve this problem.
subQuestions.memoText: Any ONE way ✓ + motivation ✓ (2 marks): WiMAX / WiFi – the hostel will be in range of WiMax / WiFi technology; fibre cable – low attenuation makes data transfer over long distances possible; UTP with switches – the signal needs to be repeatedly strengthened to cover the distance; VPN – use existing resources to securely connect to the school's network over the internet.

subQuestions.label: 3.3.1(a)
subQuestions.questionText: The school would like to incorporate VoIP technology in the classrooms. Write out the acronym VoIP.
subQuestions.memoText: Voice over Internet Protocol ✓ (1 mark)

subQuestions.label: 3.3.1(b)
subQuestions.questionText: How does VoIP differ from traditional telephone calls?
subQuestions.memoText: Any TWO differences ✓✓ (2 marks): no dedicated connection / calls made over the internet; lower cost; allows for video calls; needs preinstalled software applications; can make a call to any computing device connected to the internet; call cost not dependent on distances.

subQuestions.questionText: Assess the possible technical challenges that might be faced when using VoIP at school. Discuss at least TWO challenges.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any TWO challenges identified ✓✓ + 2 × correctly described ✓✓ (4 marks):
• Stable internet connection (1) – to ensure that the call does not disconnect (1)
• Sufficient bandwidth (1) – low connection speed can influence the quality of the call (1)
• Software (1) – must be the same version / compatible (1)
• Data cost (1) – high data cost when making video calls (1)

subQuestions.questionText: One of the short-term goals of the school is to set up an intranet. Briefly explain what an intranet is and give a practical example of how it could be used in a school environment.
subQuestions.memoText: An intranet is an organisation's private network / Internet-like environment consisting of web pages ✓. Course notes, schedules, news, announcements, etc. could be posted to the intranet, providing access to these resources / communication ✓. (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: The school received an advertisement introducing remote teaching and learning ('Work from anywhere – securely, easily and fully immersive. The ultimate remote access and work solution for remote employees, freelancers and hybrid systems'). Recommend why a remote desktop connection should be used for people working from home.
subQuestions.memoText: Any TWO reasons why an RDC should be used ✓✓ (2 marks): software is easily configured on host and target computer compared to setting up a VPN; allows users the same control on the remote device as if sitting in front of the device; changes are made to files directly on the remote computer; software is included in your operating system.

subQuestions.questionText: An example of 'remote access' is being able to access the school security while away from the school. State ONE advantage and ONE disadvantage of using remote access.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any ONE advantage ✓ (2 marks total): provides access to viewing from any location / at any time; low maintenance cost; convenient / saves time / cost saving.
Any ONE disadvantage ✓: can be hacked; setup cost is expensive; dependent on internet access / data cost; video material can take a long time to transfer.

subQuestions.questionText:
The school stores all the information of the learners in a database with multiple tables. Data was obtained from printed class lists provided by the register class teachers. The extract below is from a table called tblLearners:

ID | FirstName | Surname | Age | Gender | RegisterClass | Teacher
1 | John | Smith | 16 | Male | 10A | Boyd
2 | Jane | Doe | 18 | Female | 12C | Nkwe
3 | James | Brown | 15 | Male | 9A | Peterson
4 | Emily | Davis | 16 | Female | 10A | Boyd
5 | Michael | Johnson | 18 | Male | 12C | Nkwe

State the purpose of a primary key in a table.
subQuestions.memoText: A primary key is a field in a table that uniquely identifies each record in that table ✓. (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: State a requirement of a primary key, except not having duplicate values.
subQuestions.memoText: Cannot have a null value ✓. (1 mark)

subQuestions.label: 4.1.3(a)
subQuestions.questionText: The structure of the tblLearners table will result in anomalies. What design error in this table might lead to an anomaly?
subQuestions.memoText: Any ONE design error with explanation ✓✓ (2 marks): data is duplicated in the Teacher field (1); if the teacher is replaced, the data needs to be corrected everywhere (1). OR: the table is not normalised (1), the table contains redundant data / the Teacher field is linked to register class / the Teacher field is dependent on another field that is not part of the primary key (1). OR any TWO examples of design errors (2): data redundancy / repeated data / not normalised; a field is dependent on another field that is not the primary key / description of anomaly.

subQuestions.label: 4.1.3(b)
subQuestions.questionText: Suggest how this design error can be resolved and explain how a solution can be accomplished.
subQuestions.memoText:
Create a separate table ✓ and move the RegisterClass and Teacher fields to that table ✓. Use the RegisterClass field as the foreign key in the tblLearners table ✓ and the primary key in the new table ✓.
Concepts (4 marks): splitting the data into two tables; RegisterClass / teachers must be placed in a separate table; the tables must be linked; indication of linking on the RegisterClass. Concepts can be described or illustrated using a table diagram.

subQuestions.questionText: Data verification and data validation are important database management processes. Compare the concepts of verification and validation to clearly indicate why validation does not remove the need for verification.
subQuestions.memoText:
Validation ensures that data is acceptable / valid (1). Verification is ensuring the correctness of data (1).
Why validation does not remove the need for verification ✓✓: if data is valid, it only implies that the data is in the correct format / range / data type / presence / check digit (1) and not necessarily factually correct (1). OR: verification requires that the information be checked against the source (1), which validation does not do (1). (4 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: The school uses a 'Microsoft Access' database as their DBMS solution. What programming language is mostly used to extract data from a database?
subQuestions.memoText: SQL / Structured query language ✓ (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Identify a typical scenario when a server-based database would be required and explain how a server-based database would serve to cater for the needs of the scenario identified.
subQuestions.memoText:
Where a lot of personnel need to access the same database ✓. A server-based database will allow many users to use the database at once ✓ from many different locations ✓.
Concepts (3 marks): scenario correctly identified with many users / many locations; simultaneous use of the database / providing access to many users; access possible from different locations / over a network.

subQuestions.questionText: An audit trail is used in the school's database. How does the creation of an audit trail enhance data security in the school database?
subQuestions.memoText: Any TWO ✓✓ (2 marks): tracks WHAT changes are made; tracks WHEN changes were made; tracks WHO made changes.

subQuestions.questionText: Besides using an audit trail, suggest an alternative method to enhance the security of the school's database and explain how it can be used.
subQuestions.memoText: Any ONE method ✓ with an explanation ✓ (2 marks): access control – setting permissions and access levels for users, passwords, biometric access control, multifactor authentication, physical locking of the server room; encryption – by encrypting sensitive data such as learner records, the school can prevent unauthorised access to this information; regular backups – essential for protecting data from loss due to hardware failure, data corruption or other disasters; firewall – using a firewall to monitor all incoming and outgoing transmissions / traffic and block unwanted communication / requests.

subQuestions.label: 5.1.1(a)
subQuestions.memoText: Any ONE ✓ (1 mark): Line 1 (iCounter := 0) OR Line 4 (sLine := '')

subQuestions.label: 5.1.1(b)
subQuestions.questionText: Refer to the Delphi code extract in QUESTION 5.1. Write down the line number of any line of code from the provided code segment that implements Looping.
subQuestions.memoText: Any ONE ✓ (1 mark): Line 2 (for iRow := 1 to 3 do) OR Line 5 (for iCol := 1 to 5 do)

subQuestions.questionText: What will be the value of iCounter after the code above has been executed? (Assume that all variables are declared correctly and there are no errors in the code.)
subQuestions.memoText: 15 ✓ (1 mark)  [the inner loop runs 5 times for each of the 3 outer iterations]

subQuestions.questionText: Provide the output of the program after the code above has been executed.
subQuestions.memoText: ***** ✓ (a line of five asterisks). Only one line ✓ (redOutput.Lines.Add is outside the outer loop, so only the final value of sLine is displayed). (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: Rewrite the second loop (for iCol := 1 to 5 do) as a conditional loop.
subQuestions.memoText:
iCol := 1; ✓
while iCol <= 5 do ✓
  begin
    inc(iCol); ✓
    ...
  end;
OR: iCol := 0; (1)  repeat  inc(iCol); (1)  ...  until iCol = 5 (1)  OR any other correct solution.
Concepts (3 marks): initialise counter (1); conditional loop with correct condition (1); increment loop controller (1).

subQuestions.questionText:
A prototype application was developed for the human resources (HR) department that will allow them to search for student names. An array has been declared as follows:

    arrNames: array [1..5] of String =
        ('Trevor', 'Mpho', 'Lebo', 'Steven', 'Verushka');

The flow diagram: Start → Enter the name → counter = 0 → [Is counter <= 5?] No → Display not found → Stop; Yes → counter = counter + 1 → [Is arrNames[counter] = name?] No → back to the 'Is counter <= 5?' test; Yes → Display found → Stop.

Complete a trace table (columns: name, counter, Is counter <= 5?, Is arrNames[counter] = name?, Display) to determine the output of the flow diagram if the name 'Lebo' is the input.
subQuestions.memoText:
Trace for name = 'Lebo':
counter 0 → Is counter <= 5? True → counter 1 → Is arrNames[1] ('Trevor') = name? False → Is counter <= 5? True → counter 2 → Is arrNames[2] ('Mpho') = name? False → Is counter <= 5? True → counter 3 → Is arrNames[3] ('Lebo') = name? True → Display: Found.
Concepts (4 marks): correct counter column (1); correct 'Is counter <= 5' column (1); correct 'Is arrNames[counter] = name' column (1); correct Display – any phrase indicating 'Found' (1).

subQuestions.questionText: Write pseudocode to input a word and display the word in reverse letter order. EXAMPLE: if the word 'database' was entered as the input word, the word in reverse letter order will be displayed as 'esabatad'. The first step in the pseudocode algorithm is: Input sWord. The pseudocode must work correctly for any word that is entered, not only the word in the example.
subQuestions.memoText:
Input sWord (given)
Initialise sOutput
Loop ✓ K from length of sWord downTo 1 ✓
    sOutput ← sOutput + sWord[K] ✓✓
Display sOutput

OR: Loop K from 1 to length of sWord; sOutput ← sWord[K] + sOutput. OR any other correct solution.
Concepts (4 marks): loop (1) for the length of the word (1); correct adding of characters using correct indexing (2).

subQuestions.questionText:
An object class is required to create a student card object. The details required on the student card are: Unique student number (example: 013795); Name of the student (example: 'Trevor'); Surname of the student (example: 'Chabale'); Year of study (example: 2).

Draw a unified modelling language (UML) class diagram to represent the object class called TStudentCard. The diagram must contain: all the attributes of the TStudentCard object indicating data types and public/private scope; a constructor method indicating values received for all four attributes via a parameter list; a mutator method called setStudyYear to receive a new year of study as a parameter.
subQuestions.memoText:
TStudentCard
- fStudentNumber : String
- fName : String
- fSurname : String
- fStudyYear : integer
+ <<constructor>> Create(sStudentNumber, sName, sSurname : String; iStudyYear : integer)
+ setStudyYear(iStudyYear : integer)

Concepts to be used within a UML diagram (6 marks): indicate attributes to be private ✓; indicate methods to be public ✓; all attributes declared correctly with correct data types ✓; constructor / Create method declared correctly ✓ with correct parameters ✓; mutator method declared correctly with the correct integer parameter ✓.

subQuestions.questionText: Open days at schools are used to take learners on tours where they can see the facilities of the institution. Registration for an open-day event at a school takes place by using QR (quick response) codes to open a link to a form. The information entered on the form is then used to e-mail an application form to the learner. Explain what a QR code is and how it can be captured.
subQuestions.memoText: The use of an image / two-dimensional block code to store information / URL ✓. It can be captured / scanned using a digital camera / smartphone ✓. (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: When completing a form online, it often happens that personal information, such as your e-mail address, is automatically entered into the fields. How does that happen?
subQuestions.memoText: Any ONE ✓ (1 mark): autocomplete / autofill done by the browser; information stored in a cookie from previous visits to the site; a device / app feature from registered / stored information.

subQuestions.label: 6.2.1(a)
subQuestions.questionText: A video of a 3D tour of the school campus is placed on the school's website for learners who cannot attend the open day. A computer with the latest operating system and multiprocessing specifications was used to create the video. Explain what multiprocessing is.
subQuestions.memoText: A computer's OS utilises more than one processor or processing core ✓ to simultaneously execute multiple tasks / threads / processes ✓. (2 marks)

subQuestions.label: 6.2.1(b)
subQuestions.questionText: Discuss how the different processes are managed by the operating system to ensure that all applications will have adequate resources.
subQuestions.memoText:
The process of ensuring that each process / task / thread gets enough CPU time ✓ and access to memory, storage and other hardware ✓ to be able to work without interference by other processes.
Concepts (2 marks): allocation / sharing of processing time; allocation of resources / memory / storage.

subQuestions.questionText: When a person visits the school's website more than once, it opens much faster because of the web cache. Explain the process of web-caching.
subQuestions.memoText:
When a website is visited for the first time, the browser downloads all the necessary content from the server to cache on local storage ✓. When the user visits the website again, the browser loads the content from cache ✓.
Concepts (2 marks): web content from previous visits is stored; content obtained from the cache / local storage when visited again.

subQuestions.questionText: The online 3D tour can be downloaded or streamed. Critically discuss the increased use of streaming material rather than downloading. (Discuss at least TWO aspects, comparing the implications for both streaming and downloading.)
subQuestions.memoText:
2 × 2 marks ✓✓✓✓. Aspects (streaming vs downloading):
• Storage – streaming: accessible without needing to store locally / downloading: requires enough storage space
• Speed of access – streaming: instantly available to start watching / downloading: needs to be downloaded first
• Internet dependency – streaming: only available with an internet connection / downloading: can be viewed offline after download
• Ownership / copyright – streaming: no permanent ownership / downloading: user keeps a local copy
• Cost – streaming: often subscription models / downloading: one-time purchases or rentals
• Environmental impact – streaming: consumes more energy as it is downloaded every time it is viewed / downloading: less energy as it can be repeatedly viewed after one download
• Quality of experience – streaming: may fluctuate with internet speed / downloading: consistent quality
• Security – streaming: content only retained in a buffer / downloading: locally stored and might include malware
Also accept other relevant and correct answers.

subQuestions.questionText: The school's website is an example of a Web 1.0 generation website. State TWO characteristics of a Web 1.0 website.
subQuestions.memoText: Any TWO ✓✓ (2 marks): static pages that do not change frequently; simple design with limited graphics and multimedia content; the user is a content consumer and not a content creator; hyperlinks to other webpages for further information; basic HTML and CSS code used for webpage creation; no interactive or collaborative features, such as user comments or social media integration.

subQuestions.questionText: Give any TWO reasons that led to websites evolving from Web 1.0 to Web 2.0.
subQuestions.memoText: Any TWO ✓✓ (2 marks): to allow users to contribute content; to provide an interactive experience; to allow for social networking; availability of new web technologies; higher bandwidth availability; internet availability.

subQuestions.questionText: All the data of the prospective learners are saved in an online database. The following variations of data were recorded in the Grade field for different surnames: Chetty → '7'; Franklin → 'seven'; Gumede → 'Gr. 7'; Venter → 'Grade 7'. Discuss why the data above might compromise the quality of input data.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any TWO ✓✓ (2 marks): because of the different formats used to enter the same information / data not standardised; it will be difficult to group / compare / analyse / sort records with different formats; difficult to extract core information, which can lead to errors.
Concepts: different formats can lead to (1) incorrect capturing of data OR difficulty in extracting / interpreting the data (1).

subQuestions.questionText: State TWO different techniques on how the form, in which the data is captured, could be optimised to prevent this type of input.
subQuestions.memoText: Any TWO ✓✓ (2 marks): selection components (list box; combo box / dropdown box; radio group; spin edit); providing examples of the required format / default values; input mask.

subQuestions.questionText: Data gathered from a form needs to be used for decision-making. The process of transforming data in the information cycle is depicted as: Data → (a) → (b) → Decisions. Provide the missing labels for parts (a) and (b).
subQuestions.memoText:
(a) ✓ and (b) ✓ (2 marks).
Alternative 1: (a) Information; (b) Knowledge.
Alternative 2: (a) Processing; (b) Information / Knowledge.

subQuestions.questionText: The school is one of many schools in the 'LearnMore School' franchise enrolling new learners. A distributed database is used to save the data required for use by the school. Why would a distributed database be a more suitable option for this scenario?
subQuestions.memoText: Any ONE ✓ (1 mark): increased performance levels / less traffic on the network / less traffic on the server / less data transfer; can accommodate many users; needs to be accessed from many locations; more stable (reduces redundancy).

subQuestions.questionText: Private information that is transferred over public networks, such as the internet, should always be encrypted. Briefly explain how encryption works.
subQuestions.memoText: The information is scrambled / made inaccessible ✓ using a secret key / algorithm / set of rules ✓. (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: Suggest which distributed database model will be most suitable for this scenario and motivate your answer.
subQuestions.memoText:
Partitioning ✓ – each server only stores the part of the data it works with / less data to be stored or transferred ✓.
OR: duplication (1) – every server holds all the data / data will not be lost if one server crashes (1). (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: Technology has made it possible for more people to gain access to information. Give TWO examples of digital communication platforms that can be used to promote the open-day event of the school.
subQuestions.memoText: Any TWO valid digital platforms ✓✓ (2 marks): email; social media; blogs; online newspapers; instant messaging; website. Also accept any TWO examples of any of the above.

subQuestions.questionText: It has been reported that confidential information about parents and learners has been distributed without their knowledge. Which policy document can be used as motivation for the need to take disciplinary action against the perpetrator?
subQuestions.memoText: Any ONE ✓ (1 mark): Acceptable Usage Policy (AUP); Privacy Policy; POPIA; EULA (End User License Agreement).

subQuestions.questionText: The school decided to host a workshop on artificial intelligence (AI) and invited the primary school learners to attend. ChatGPT as an AI tool is frequently used to generate information based on user input. State TWO potential risks associated with the use of ChatGPT.
subQuestions.memoText: Any TWO ✓✓ (2 marks): people rely on the information generated without any fact-checking; copyright issues / plagiarism; over-reliance on the technology; replacing human skills / employment opportunities; removing motivation to learn skills; limited accountability; may generate potentially inappropriate content for children; may generate malicious code; may track and store personal information. Also accept other valid examples.
